🔍 Google Pixel 11 lineup details leak

Google plans to launch four Pixel 11 models: Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Screen sizes and resolutions remain similar to the previous generation, but brightness will increase to 3100 nits on the base model and 3600 nits on Pro versions. The foldable model features dual screens with 3600 nits outside and 3500 nits inside.

The Pixel 11 series runs on the new Tensor G6 chip built on a 2nm TSMC process, featuring a seven-core CPU with an ARM C1-Ultra core at 4.11 GHz, PowerVR graphics, Titan M3 security chip, and MediaTek M90 modem. Storage starts at 256 GB, eliminating the 128 GB option and raising the entry price to match last year's 256 GB model.

🤖 Grok can now build and publish apps from a single prompt

Describe an idea, and Grok will generate a working web app, publish it, and give it its own domain, all in minutes.

The new Build Mode works on the web, iPhone, and Android. Behind the scenes, Grok uses a coding agent with specialized subagents, browser tools, and Grok Imagine for image generation.

You can build dashboards, productivity tools, games, and other web apps, then keep them on a Grok domain, connect your own custom domain, or export the full source code to GitHub.

For now, Build Mode is available exclusively to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers.

🤖 ChatGPT just became a lot more personal with Health mode

OpenAI has launched Health mode, allowing ChatGPT to connect with your Apple Health data and medical records to provide answers based on your actual health information, not just general advice.

Users can link Apple Health, One Medical, or Function Health to share blood tests, medications, doctor visits, sleep, workouts, and other health data. ChatGPT can then compare test results over time, explain medical terms, and even recommend allergy-safe restaurants based on your profile.

OpenAI says around 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions every week, with most conversations starting outside dedicated health chats. Health mode brings that context directly into everyday conversations.

Free users get GPT-5.5 Instant, which can recognize when it’s time to see a real doctor. Paid users get GPT-5.6 Sol, offering deeper analysis and more detailed explanations for complex health questions.
